title: Morning Headlines
intro: A possible U.S.-Iran peace deal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz tops a packed Sunday, alongside a joint strike on a major gang leader, World Cup drama, and a landmark physics result.

items.title: Trump Says Iran Peace Deal Set for Today; Tehran Disputes Timing
items.subtitle: Al Jazeera / CBS News / NPR
items.summary: President Trump declared on Truth Social that a ceasefire agreement with Iran — including immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and steps to dismantle Iran's nuclear program — would be signed Sunday, while Iranian officials said a finalized pact was unlikely so soon. The deal, brokered with Pakistani mediation, would end a conflict that has roiled global energy markets since earlier this year.

items.title: U.S. and Venezuela Kill Top Tren de Aragua Leader in Joint Strike
items.subtitle: CBS News / CNN / NPR
items.summary: A joint U.S.-Venezuela military operation killed Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores — 'Niño Guerrero' — who led the Tren de Aragua transnational gang for over a decade, growing it from a Venezuelan prison gang into a criminal network spanning the Americas, with CIA intelligence support. The strike signals an unusual level of security cooperation between Washington and Caracas.

items.title: Crude Oil Slides 2%, Markets Rally as Iran Deal Nears
items.subtitle: CNBC / Charles Schwab
items.summary: Global equities posted weekly gains and crude oil fell roughly 2% to near $85 a barrel as investors priced in the potential lifting of Iran oil sanctions and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for roughly 20% of global seaborne oil. A finalized deal would represent the most significant shift in global energy supply this year.

items.title: Scotland Win First World Cup Match in 36 Years, Beating Haiti 1-0
items.subtitle: ESPN
items.summary: John McGinn's deflected strike gave Scotland a historic 1-0 victory over Haiti on Day 4 of the FIFA World Cup, ending a 36-year drought stretching back to 1990. Brazil and Morocco drew 0-0 in the day's other marquee fixture, with Germany, the Netherlands, and Ivory Coast also in action.

items.title: China's JUNO Observatory Publishes Landmark Neutrino Results in Nature
items.subtitle: ScienceDaily / Scientific American / Nature
items.summary: The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory in China released its debut physics results in Nature, refining neutrino oscillation measurements by a factor of 1.6 over all prior experiments combined — using just 59 days of data from a detector the size of a ten-story building. The result puts JUNO on track to resolve which type of neutrino is lightest, one of the biggest open questions in particle physics.
